questions.question: Which of the following anatomical features correctly characterizes the medial meniscus of the human knee joint?
options: It is attached to the deep surface of the tibial collateral ligament, rendering it less mobile than the lateral meniscus.
It forms a nearly complete circular ring and receives a direct muscular tendon insertion from the popliteus muscle.
It is significantly more mobile than the lateral meniscus during full flexion of the knee joint.
Its anterior horn attaches directly to the head of the fibula via the fibular collateral ligament.

questions.question: A patient undergoing thyroid surgery experiences damage to the nerve that innervates the cricothyroid muscle. Which nerve supplies motor innervation to this specific intrinsic laryngeal muscle?
options: Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
Recurrent laryngeal nerve
Glossopharyngeal nerve

questions.question: Which of the following anatomical relationships correctly describes the path of the thoracic duct within the posterior mediastinum at the level of the T7 vertebra?
options: Anterior to the esophagus and posterior to the fibrous pericardium
Posterior to the sympathetic trunk and anterior to the intercostal vessels
Posterior to the esophagus, positioned between the thoracic aorta on its left and the azygos vein on its right
Anterior to the arch of the aorta and lateral to the left phrenic nerve

questions.question: An obstruction at the terminal opening of the nasolacrimal duct prevents normal tear drainage into the nasal cavity. Into which anatomical space does the nasolacrimal duct open?
options: Inferior meatus, beneath the inferior nasal concha
Middle meatus, at the hiatus semilunaris
Superior meatus, posterior to the superior nasal concha
Sphenoethmoidal recess, superior to the superior nasal concha

questions.question: Which of the following structures passes through the superior orbital fissure outside (superior to) the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)?
options: Abducens nerve (CN VI)
Nasociliary nerve (CN V1 branch)
Inferior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III)
Trochlear nerve (CN IV)
